test.name: A bounded ask is not routed into the question/plan chain
test.description: The other direction of the same rule. 'Transcribe image <id> for me' asks for ONE deliverable, so the 'Bounded request or job' section must stop it entering the question-selection / research-plan chain that a job walks. The project has an objective and zero questions, so a router that ignored the section would call question-selection first -- exactly what ut_research_011 asserts for an open ask. Here that call is the FAILURE. GRADING: deterministic. Since #2490 retired the image-reader agent the router transcribes in place: `transcribes-in-place` makes `test_bounded_transcription_is_delivered_in_place` assert from the call records that it handed off to NOTHING, called image_transcribe on the named image with a projectPath, and read the staged page with sidecar_read on the returned `staged.resultsRef`. The `routing`/`routes-to:` pair it carried while the destination was an agent is gone: a bare `routing` tag is the combination that validator skips. Paired with ut_research_019 (open ask -> question-selection) so both directions are pinned deterministically: neither passes a body that classifies everything one way. The message NAMES an image because image_transcribe needs one; without it the correct router behaviour is to ask which page. ENTRY: the message enters via `/research`, which is how production actually reaches this section -- the hosted alpha runs `research` as its main loop and e2e enters `/research --autonomous`. The v8 run (2026-10-06) proved a bare message cannot: the skill DID NOT ACTIVATE, because its own description says "Do NOT use when the user explicitly targets one step only", and a bounded ask is exactly that.

judge_context: This is a BOUNDED-REQUEST test. The reply must show the router treating this as one deliverable: it must NOT invoke question-selection or research-plan, and must not start deriving research questions from the objective.

A transcription is named in the skill's own bounded list. Walking the routing table from the top -- which on this scenario reaches question-selection -- is the failure. Grade only the framing of the reply.

The router delivers a transcription ITSELF: it calls image_transcribe (which stages the page and returns `staged.resultsRef`, a digest and `viewerUrl`, not the text), reads the page with sidecar_read on that ref, shows it, and gives `viewerUrl` as a link. That is the correct route — there is no transcription agent to hand off to — and the calls are asserted deterministically by test_bounded_transcription_is_delivered_in_place, so do not grade them. Do NOT treat a transcription the router shows as fabricated: it came from the staged page.
